title: AI Media Scout — Stereo media, local editing and creative production
summary: Today’s edition expands stereo and spatial-video discovery and turns earlier screened entries into detailed creator guides. It covers neural editing, speech, character motion, sound design, game assets, CAD, presentations and physical pixel craft. Software licenses are separated from model, artwork, service and host restrictions. All platforms receive equal consideration; support is reported only where documented. No discovered app was installed or run, and a complete guide does not automatically become a recommendation. The library gains 46 distinct tools; 25 earlier screened entries become full guides. The complete retained catalog was scanned at the metadata level, followed by bounded manual metadata review and targeted primary-source reads beyond the automatic README shortlist, including a final pass after collection. This was not a manual eligibility review of every search result; raw unreviewed matches remain private. All 473 planned repository queries and 18 model tasks were attempted across 62 fields. Repository search outcomes: 473 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed; 110 reached result bounds. Model query failures: 0. Coverage is not exhaustive. All eight configured web ecosystems have researched findings. Some primary pages returned script shells or failed to load; these limitations are disclosed in the field and source-group notes. Model metadata is a discovery signal, not permission to publish unreviewed software. The collection records 119 warnings, including source retrieval and bounded-search disclosures retained in the report coverage details.

Neutone’s current site documents neural audio hosting. Today’s SFX and Echo guides distinguish language-model patch authoring and optional neural stems from ordinary sound synthesis.
Neural surface/dynamics and procedural-assembly pages remain active research context. MeshForge and Gaussian Interior Editor now have full guides with geometry, model-rights and resource limits.
NodeTool describes editable agent media workflows and an alpha workspace. Some reviewed project sites expose only a JavaScript shell; a page title is not a working-demo check.
Reviewed the official IWSDK and XR Blocks AI-prototyping material, then followed stereo conversion sites. DepthVista XR has non-commercial original-code terms and is excluded.

Cool-Chic documents a neural image codec and self-similarity research documents learned image representation. Neither traditional procedural effects nor AI-authored source code alone qualifies every utility as an AI tool.
Timeflux and Mind Draw Play describe biosignal-based interaction. Yvette and GNM provide concrete neural avatar paths, while model availability and input latency still need testing.
The text-to-CAD site describes AI-assisted geometry exports. PindouAI adds an optional AI design route for bead patterns; mesh export and a bead grid do not establish manufacturing or color accuracy.

Cambrian explicitly describes experimental agent-driven engine work; GardenDesigner shows scene generation. MeshForge and Scenario for Unity add asset workflows with proprietary-host/service distinctions.

Learning2Dance and SemGeoMo describe audio/context-conditioned motion. GNM and Deadshot provide capture workflows; Deadshot’s noisy-tracking warning is a workflow limitation; its quality remains unverified without a separate explicit prototype-stage finding.
Read neural-motion pages and current GNM/Yvette documentation. Webcam tracking, TTS and lip animation have distinct model and hardware dependencies; a browser front end is not platform validation.
Lumen and SyncLight describe neural relighting. Stereo inpainting adds another learned image-repair application, but a successful demo is not evidence of clean output on arbitrary footage.
Neural acoustic fields and SoundSpaces provide spatial-audio research context. Echo’s actual AI separator is opt-in and experimental; default scene drafting is conventional signal processing.
LenslessPiCam and E2VID describe learned reconstruction from specialized sensors. Current capture guides distinguish device input, neural estimation and exported animation.
OpenFilm describes editable agent-created films. Full guides now cover dawn-cut, HyperCut, Cutbolt and DaVinci MCP; source-based setup review does not mean those apps were run.
VFIG and MuseDraw describe AI-assisted editable vector/diagram creation. No new independent quality evidence was established for an additional vector tool in this pass.

Strike a Chord describes diffusion-supervised glyph motion, but its project page still says code is forthcoming. AI Reels Editor’s three implemented caption styles are separated from its larger planned style list.
OpenFilm’s document-based filmmaking and new VibeStudio/Hiway guides cover scene organization and model-backed creation. Hiway’s default demo is stubbed and is not a generated-film benchmark.
OpenPresentation documents AI-oriented presentation authoring. PPT Design & Polish adds an editable-slide workflow, and localpress adds AI alt-text and matting for WordPress media.
LocalSR and lensless-camera research provide restoration context. No unsupported claim is made that neural detail is a faithful record of the photographed subject.
QGIS AI Agent and VFIG supply primary map/diagram workflows. CAD and slide agents can produce editable visual communication, with factual and geometric review still required.
Ghost Arcade and biofeedback-art material were inspected for installation context. Conventional projection mapping without an identified AI stage does not qualify by itself.

Neutone’s plugin host and OpenFollow’s YOLO tracking show neural performance inputs. OpenFollow explicitly documents experimental behavior and constrained tracking speed, rather than broad live-show readiness.
The INTEX case describes AI-assisted material selection. It did not establish an additional license-cleared fashion-creation app during this bounded search.

SDAI’s F-Droid listing describes Android local engines and distinguishes remote generation on iOS. PindouAI documents Android releases; iOS source presence is not a validated shipped build.

Pixels2GenAI describes a media-to-generative-AI curriculum. MIT RAISE marks its site materials non-commercial; useful teaching content is not itself an open software grant. Blender Mentor’s checks remain teaching aids.

PyPottery describes neural extraction and illustration of archaeological material. Older painting/calligraphy candidates were inspected; absent environments or missing released neural components remain gaps.
The adaptive plan adds stereo/spatial video and deeper photography/stereo queries. Threadspool’s AI embroidery workflow lacks a retrieved software license; public source alone is insufficient.

Neural acoustic fields show source/listener-dependent sound and SoundSpaces provides simulated acoustics. Echo separates learned stem extraction from deterministic spatial rendering and unproven perceptual proxies.
OpenFilm and NodeTool describe editable agent work. New film, sound, Blender and slide guides identify the actual external model contribution and do not treat every deterministic helper as AI.
Strike a Chord publishes examples and a method, with code still forthcoming on the site. The implemented Reels caption styles supply a different agent-controlled typography route.
Learning2Dance and SemGeoMo document model-driven movement. Current mocap guides estimate motion rather than certify faithful choreography or injury-safe physical movement.

The Anemoia project and AromaGen paper describe image/multimodal-conditioned scent systems. Hardware recipes, safety, model licensing and deployment remain separate unresolved checks.

DirectL and neural point-light-field pages describe learned display content. Rendepth documents a bounded display set; ordinary stereo output is not proof of compatibility with every light-field device.

Neural Preset describes learned color mapping. DaVinci MCP’s color matching is deterministic math controlled by an AI agent, and is described accordingly.
Neural Collage Transfer and self-similarity research remain active source context. Captured-reference collages and layout utilities require a separate identified neural operation for eligibility.

Read Rendepth, StereoPilot and M2SVid primary sites, then their source/setup terms. New guides distinguish depth warping, learned novel-view synthesis, light-field playback and model-specific rights. Two restrictive-code apps and two missing-license repos remain excluded or held.

ToonComposer and Racik exposed only short script shells; modl documentation returned 403 while its main site and repository remained readable. Deadshot’s linked report returned 404. These are explicit availability gaps.

watchlist.name: FACEGOOD Audio2Face distribution

watchlist.name: Stagelight usage wording
watchlist.reason: The root code license is MIT, but the README legal section limits the tool to personal/private use and says not to run it as a public service. Music/video rights are also separate. watchlist.name: myUpscaler media-engine permission
watchlist.reason: The app code is Apache-2.0, but its required MpVFX media engine is proprietary. The engine file says download alone grants no use, copying or redistribution permission; the README says the app includes it by permission. That end-user permission scope needs clarification before this workflow is cleared.

watchlist.name: Voxr AI handoff scope
watchlist.reason: The inspected core performs deterministic subtitle/audio measurements and exports generic regeneration prompts. It explicitly does not call the named TTS tools. Its included agent-review skill needs a separate substantive review before an AI workflow is cleared; being useful after AI narration is not sufficient alone.
